steps.body: A bar drawing turns a length story into geometry: one bar per quantity, aligned starts, and the picture asks its own question.
steps.narration: A bar drawing turns a length story into geometry: one bar per quantity, aligned starts, and the picture asks its own question.

widget.prompt: The story's two bars, aligned: which quantity is longer?
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — after the starts align, trail A reaches farther.

predict.prompt: In a bar drawing, what does a GAP between bar ends mean?
predict.reveal: The gap is the picture's question — the difference between the quantities the bars represent.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p draw model.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p draw model.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: A drawing shows a 60 cm bar. Under it, a 24 cm bar and a 16 cm bar sit end to end, plus a mystery piece reaching the same end. What is the mystery piece?

options.label: The missing length: 60 − 24 − 16 = 20 cm
options.feedback: Correct — the three lower parts must rebuild the 60 cm bar: 24 + 16 = 40, and 20 more fills the gap.

options.label: The total: 60 + 24 + 16 = 100 cm
options.feedback: The rows END together, so the lower row equals 60 — nothing in the drawing stacks to 100.

options.label: 40 cm — the two known parts joined
options.feedback: 24 + 16 = 40 is the part already drawn; the mystery piece is what is LEFT: 60 − 40 = 20.

options.label: It cannot be found from a drawing
options.feedback: Equal ends make it findable — the picture is the equation 24 + 16 + ? = 60.

widget.prompt: The pine branch measures 50 cm and the oak branch measures 39 cm. How much longer is the pine branch?

commonErrors.feedback: That joined the two lengths — "how much longer" wants the gap between them, found by subtracting.
The gap came out two too wide; align the lengths end to end and recount the extra.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.

widget.prompt: A drawing shows two bars placed end to end: a 26 cm piece, then a 17 cm piece. What is the total length of the two pieces stacked together?

options.label: The total: 26 + 17 = 43 cm
options.feedback: Correct — placing the two pieces end to end joins their lengths, so the total is 43 cm.

options.label: The difference: 26 − 17 = 9 cm
options.feedback: Subtracting finds a GAP between two ends, not the combined length of two joined pieces.

options.label: Only the longer piece: 26 cm
options.feedback: That ignores the second piece entirely — a total must include every piece that was joined.

options.label: Another copy of the 26 cm piece: 52 cm
options.feedback: The second piece measures 17 cm, not another 26 cm copy — use each piece's own length.

hints: Place both known pieces end to end.
Joining two pieces means adding, not subtracting.
The total collects every piece that was placed.

widget.prompt: A drawing shows a 30 cm bar on top. Under it, an 18 cm bar and a mystery piece reach the same end. How long is the mystery piece?

options.label: The gap it fills: 30 − 18 = 12 cm
options.feedback: Correct — the two lower parts rebuild the 30 cm bar, so the mystery piece fills the 12 cm gap.

options.label: The sum of the bars: 30 + 18 = 48 cm
options.feedback: The bars END together, so they match — nothing in the drawing stacks to 48.

options.label: A twin of the 18 cm bar: 18 cm
options.feedback: Two 18s make 36 and overshoot the 30 cm bar by 6 — the ends would no longer meet.

options.label: No drawing can name its length
options.feedback: The drawing is what makes it findable — equal ends turn the picture into an equation.
